rows.en: Whatever I do, it's wasted effort
Just then, I suddenly remembered Arai's story.{p}

The story about the principal choosing the students who would become sacrifices.
{f:By rights|By rights}, {f:I|I} was never meant to come to this school {f:at all|at all}.
The principal had manipulated things, and that was why {f:I|I} {f:ended up|ended up} passing the entrance exam.
{f:If so|In that case}, going to the principal's office might tell me something.
The thought flashed through {f:my|my} mind.
{f:I|I} forced my heavy, sluggish body up and decided to go to the school.{p}

Maybe because I had been shut up in the house for so long, the midday sun was painful for {f:me|me}.
It was as if even the sun was trying to get in {f:my|my} way.
I nearly {f:gave up|gave up} then and there.
Even so, {f:I|I} summoned the last of my strength and dragged my heavy feet to school.{p}

The school was astonishingly quiet.
The sports teams should have been out practicing.
Had they {f:all|all} taken the day off together?
And hadn't the demolition of the old school building started {f:by now|by now}?
{f:If so|If so}, I should have been hearing the racket of construction.
...But none of that mattered to {f:me|me} now.
{f:I|I} had come to school for just one reason.
To go to the principal's {f:office|office}.{p}

I arrived in front of the principal's office.
It was strange that I hadn't run into anyone at {f:all|all}.
But that was fine.
If anyone had seen {f:my|my} face as it was now, they would surely have mistaken me for a ghost.
I put my hand on the doorknob of the principal's office.
For some reason, it wasn't locked.
It felt just like a trap.
What should I {f:do|do}?{p}Should I go {f:in|in}?
Go in
Don't go in
As you'd expect of a principal's office, the inside was lavishly furnished.{p}Where should I {f:look|look}?
Shelf
Shelf
Desk
Desk
Top of the desk
Umbrella stand
Umbrella stand
Wardrobe
Wardrobe

{f:I|I} examined the top of the desk.
A neatly organized desk.
On it sat an expensive-looking pen case and a single framed portrait.
{f:I|I} casually picked up the portrait.{p}

Two happy-looking people were in the picture.
{f:Probably|Probably} a father and son.
Now that I thought about it, {f:I|I} had never seen the principal.
He was famous for rarely showing himself in public, and I remembered he hadn't even given a speech at the entrance ceremony.
Was this kind-looking middle-aged man the {f:principal|principal}?
{f:I|I} let my eyes rest on the boy who seemed to be his son, and froze in shock.{p}

...Shoji Arai.
The boy smiling in that photo was, without a doubt, Shoji Arai.
And then {f:I|I} remembered.
The principal's surname was Arai.
How had I never {f:noticed|noticed} until now?{p}
{f:My|My} hand holding the portrait trembled, and I dropped it.{p}

The glass shattered, and a key fell out from inside.
What could this key {f:be for|be for}?{p}
{f:I|I} picked up the key.{p}
Then I took another good look at the fallen photo.{p}

...So {f:Arai|Arai} was a real person {f:after all|after all}.
And of all things, he was the principal's {f:son|son}.{p}
But then, why?
Why had {f:Arai|Arai} posed as a student at this school and told {f:us|us} those {f:stories|stories}?{p}
Just who {f:was|was} he?{p}

There was no point in standing here {f:thinking|thinking}.
{f:I|I} decided to search elsewhere.{p}Where should I look?
Shelf
Shelf
Desk
Top of the desk
Umbrella stand
Umbrella stand
Wardrobe
Wardrobe
{f:I|I} decided to check the desk drawer.{p}

{f:I|I} slid the key from the portrait into the drawer's keyhole.
A perfect fit.{p}
Inside the drawer, behind some complicated-looking documents, lay an old diary, as if someone had hidden it there.{p}Should I read {f:it|it}?
Read it
Don't read it

19XX, August 9.
Today, Shoji died.
He was only seventeen.
Shoji did nothing wrong.
It was a cerebral hemorrhage.
Why did Death choose Shoji?
I curse God.{p}

August 24.
I cannot forget Shoji.
When I close my eyes, Shoji's smile rises before me on its own, and his laughter fills my ears.
I cannot forget Shoji.
If Shoji could come back to life, I would do anything.{p}

October 7.
With each passing day, my memories of Shoji spread further within me.
At last, I decided to have a certain renowned doll maker make a doll of Shoji.
If this doll can take Shoji's place, perhaps my heart will lighten a little.{p}

November 30.
The new doll arrived, but once again I am not satisfied.
This is not Shoji.
It is just a doll.
I want a doll that can take Shoji's place.{p}

February 3.
The failed dolls keep piling up.
Not one of them is Shoji.
My Shoji.
Shoji is my reason for living.
If Shoji comes back to life, I need nothing else.
I will offer up my own life, too.{p}
February 5.

I have decided to sell my soul to the devil.
I have succeeded in making a pact with the devil.
If I offer up the soul of one child every year from now on, then in thirteen years Shoji's soul will dwell in the doll, and he will be able to live again.
That is enough for me.
From now on, one sacrifice every year...{p}

As I read that far into the diary, {f:I|I} found a small key between the pages.
What could this key {f:be for|be for}?{p}

{f:Still|Anyway}, if it was tucked away in a place like {f:this|this}, it {f:had to be|had to be} a very important key.
{f:I|I} quietly slipped the key into my pocket.{p}

Just then.
The door I was sure I had closed slowly began to open.{p}

"So you're the last sacrifice, are you?
I thought you might be turning up about now.
Some of the sacrifices sneak into this office just before they die.
So I decided to wait.
And you turned out to be just the same.
Hee hee..."
So the principal {f:had|had} been offering a sacrifice to the devil every year to bring his son back to life.{p}

{f:I|I} glanced at the doll standing silently beside me.
{f:Arai|Arai} had said this year's sacrifice would be the last.
Then if {f:I|I} died, {f:would|would} this doll come back to life as Shoji Arai?
No {f:way|way}.
{f:I am who I am|I am who I am}.
{f:Like hell I'm going to die|I don't want to die}!{p}

"Now, now, there's nothing to be afraid of.
There's nothing frightening at all.
Even if you die, you'll be reborn right away.
Now die for Shoji, won't you!"{p}

The principal charged at {f:me|me}, swinging the golf club around wildly.
What should I {f:do|do}?{p}Where do I run★
Umbrella stand
Shelf
Under the desk
Wardrobe
Out of the principal's office

{f:I|I} leaped toward the wardrobe on instinct.
The moment I did, the principal {f:stopped dead in his tracks|froze on the spot}.
"Get away! Get away from that wardrobe!"
After that, the principal kept his distance from {f:me|me} and didn't attack.
There {f:must|must} be something terribly precious inside this wardrobe.
{f:I|I} grabbed the handle.
...But it was locked and wouldn't open.{p}What should I {f:do|do}?
Bang on the wardrobe
Knock the wardrobe over
Press my ear to the wardrobe
Run somewhere else

When I listened closely, I could hear some kind of sound coming from inside the wardrobe.
{f:I|I} pressed my ear against the wardrobe without thinking.
From inside came a sound like something crawling around.
When {f:I|I} pushed it into the keyhole, the principal came at {f:me|me}, screaming.{p}

{f:I|I} turned the key and flung the wardrobe doors wide open.
And then...{p}

There was a dull thud, and the principal's golf club struck the thing inside the wardrobe.
"Ah... ah... Shoji, Shoji..."
The principal stood quaking, his eyes riveted on the inside of the wardrobe.
The club slipped limply from the principal's hand.
The head of the club was smeared thick with red blood.
A nose-curling stench came drifting out of the wardrobe.
{f:I|I} carefully peered into the wardrobe.{p}

"Urrgh!"
The stench and the sight were so overwhelming that {f:I|I} threw up everything in my stomach.
Inside the wardrobe was a thing like the doll that had always been at {f:my|my} side.
And that thing's head had been smashed open by the club.
The thing inside the wardrobe had brown skin wrapped in a yellow-green mucous membrane, and it was trembling weakly in tiny, jerking spasms.

"I'll kill you!"
Just then, the principal lunged at {f:me|me}.
"It was you!
You killed Shoji!"
...Stop it.
He's going to kill me!
Just then, an eerie voice rang out.{p}

"My contract is hereby concluded."
The moment the voice was heard, the principal screamed.{p}
As if I were watching a film on fast-forward, the blood drained from the principal's face and his whole body withered away like a mummy.{p}

Then, in an instant, he was nothing but skin and bones, and he crumbled.
He hit the floor and shattered, and not even a corpse was left, only a heap of sand.
...The contract is over?
The contract with a devil{f:?|?}{p}

"Gack!"
At that moment...
Suddenly, {f:I|I} was being strangled from behind.
What {f:the hell|is this}{f:|}★{p}
I forcibly twisted my neck around and looked back over my shoulder. The doll with the split head was strangling {f:me|me}.{p}

"Let's... play... Let's... play..."
This strength was beyond anything a doll should have{f:.|.}
There was no way I could shake it off.
What {f:do I do|should I do}!
Am {f:I|I} going to die like this{f:?|?}{p}And just when I'd felt the will to live welling up inside my body...
Thrust my hand into the doll's split head
Pull the doll's head off
Tear up the diary
Throw the sand that was once the principal at the doll
When I dragged the doll down out of the wardrobe, it had turned back into an ordinary doll.{p}
Before I knew it, it had turned back into an ordinary doll.{p}

"{f:Whoa|Eek}!"
{f:I|I} leapt up in a panic.
Spiders as big as the palm of my hand came skittering out of the doll's split head{f:.|!}
Every one of those spiders had a human face.
One, two... eleven, twelve.
There were twelve human-faced spiders in all.
{f:Were these|Could these be} the souls of all the students who had been sacrificed until now?
As the spiders crawled out of the head, they vanished as if melting into the air.{p}

{f:I|I} happened to glance down at the torn diary.
I hadn't noticed it before, but a slip of paper had been tucked inside.{p}
And what would the police make of the broken doll with its lower half still inside the wardrobe{f:?|?}
And the broken doll in the principal's office... how would anyone explain that{f:?|...}

No one would believe {f:my|my} story anyway{f:.|.}
I'd like to run this as the seventh story in the school paper's special feature{f:, but|, but}... that project stalled after that day, didn't it.{p}

Even outside the principal's office, everything was so quiet.
{f:I|I} dragged my heavy legs down the empty hallway and headed home.{p}
...And about a month went by.{p}
Didn't he want to tell {f:us|us} something{f:?|?}{p}

"Um, everyone...
Won't you stay here a little longer?
I just kind of feel like it..."
{f:I|I} ventured.{p}

"What? Give me a break.
We get put in this awful mood, and on top of that you want us to stay here?"
Hosoda started complaining.
He had a point{f:.|, didn't he.}
I had no reason to keep them here{f:.|.}
{f:I|I} said,
"...I'm sorry.
I didn't really mean anything by it...
I just got a little worried about that story.
I thought maybe we should talk about what to do from here on...
So I just..."{p}

"No, it's fine.
You were worried about us, right?
We're all friends now, after all.
Don't make that face.
Nobody's going to die.
Well, {f:I'm heading home|see you next time}."{p}

{f:I|I} tensed my shoulders.
Wait {f:a sec|a minute}...
No way, th-the doll★
Showing up with timing this perfect isn't fair!
I could feel a presence behind me that sent chills down my spine.
Should I just make a run for it{f:?|?}
That's {f:the only way|all I can do}!
"Eek!"
At that moment, {f:it|it} grabbed {f:my|my} shoulder hard.
Then it forced {f:me|me} to turn around.{p}
"Help me.........{f:Huh|Jeez}, it's just you, Fukuzawa."{p}

"Oh, really?
What a shame, after I waited for you and everything.
I know, I'll go ahead and wait for you at the side entrance.
Is that still a no?"
Fukuzawa wasn't one to give up easily.
"Okay, fine{f:.|.}
Then {f:I|I}'ll hurry and return it, and we'll meet up there."
{f:I|I} gave in to her pushiness.{p}

Suddenly I saw what looked like a human figure at the corner up ahead.
...I could sense something there.{p}

"Fukuzawa☆"
{f:I|I} clung to her back without thinking.
"{c}{f:|}★
What's wrong★
Grabbing on to me all of a sudden like that."
I could still hear the footsteps.
Couldn't she see it{f:★|★}
That thing's figure, its footsteps...
{f:I|I} stayed clinging to Fukuzawa's back with my eyes shut tight.{p}

"★"
The figure from before was pressed flat against the edge of that corner.
And it was looking at {f:me|me}, with Fukuzawa between us.
It was faintly lit by the green glow of the emergency lights.
{f:I|I} walked faster so that {f:it|it} wouldn't come into view.{p}

At the end of the hallway, I could see the side entrance under its emergency light.
"Finally, the exit{f:...|...}"{p}
{f:I|I} murmured in relief.{p}

A figure★
...A figure was coming toward us from the far end.
"...{c}{f:|}.
{c}{f:|}!"
Fukuzawa's voice snapped {f:me|me} back to my senses.{p}

"If it pleases you, I should be most delighted to graciously lend you my shoulder, I do declare.
Ohohoho."
Fukuzawa laughed as she said it.
Her joke eased {f:my|my} nerves a little.
"That will not be necessary, my lady.
Come, let us be off.
One never knows what may happen in a school at night{f:...|...}"{p}
{f:I|I} thought it over after that.{p}

"Shindo!"
When I turned around, Shindo was standing there.
Shindo clenched his fist and said,
"What, you came looking for Arai too?"
{f:I|I} spoke to Shindo as if pleading with him.{p}

"{f:I|I} didn't come looking for Arai.
...Actually, Arai was never supposed to come to that meeting.
Apparently someone called Kiyose was supposed to come instead.
Yes, Hino told me.
So I went to see this Kiyose person, but...
I can't make heads or tails of any of it."{p}

Shindo came up to {f:me|me} and muttered with a sigh.
"...I see. ...I went looking for Arai, y'know."
{f:I|I} was a little startled.
"...What! Really★
And?"
It was hard to believe I was the same person who'd just been saying I wouldn't stick my nose into this{f:.|.}
"...Come over here a sec."{p}
No... I'm fine with everything staying just as it is.

Whatever I do now, it'll all end the same way{f:.|.}
Starting tomorrow, I won't go to school.
I won't take baths.
I won't eat.
I won't go to the restroom.
I won't do anything anymore.
I'll stop everything I have to do to stay alive.
If the doll is going to kill me anyway...
Everything I do to stay alive just seems ridiculous.
{f:I|I} lay down on the bed and slowly closed my eyes.{p}

Then I slowly opened them.
When I looked beside me, that doll was lying next to {f:me|me}.
Its skin was pressed flat against {f:mine|mine}.
...The doll's skin was cool, and it felt good.
That's what {f:I|I} thought, with what senses I had left.
.................................It seemed the doll's skin was warming up too, taking on the warmth of {f:my|my} skin{f:.|.}{p}

Lying on my back, I felt a single tear run from {f:my|my} eye.
Maybe because my body was so cold, the tear felt warm.
No, that's not it...
Even with my body this cold, my tears alone could still be this warm... {f:I|I} had never known that until now.{p}

I tried beckoning to the doll.
I sensed the doll lying beside me.
Here it {f:is|is}...
{f:I|I} silently questioned the doll in my heart.
({f:Who are you|Who are you}?
Why are you trying to haunt {f:me|me} to death{f:?|?}){p}

(...It's... enough now.
...I just... want to rest...
If... it stays... like this...)
I heard the voice in broken fragments.
...I couldn't quite make it out.
But {f:my|my} attempt had worked.
{f:I|I} had managed to talk with the doll, heart to heart{f:.|!}
But {f:I|I} didn't understand what it meant.
And the doll seemed a little different from how it had been before.
It wore a strange expression {f:I|I}'d never seen on it.{p}
